items.prompt: What does an O(n) claim alone establish?

options.text: The code takes exactly n CPU cycles
options.why: Big-O does not identify exact costs or hardware.

options.text: Its runtime is identical on all data distributions
options.why: Input shape/case can change actual work.

options.text: It is faster than every O(n²) program for every n
options.why: Constants and small inputs can reverse finite-size timings.

options.text: An eventual upper growth bound under stated assumptions
options.why: Tightness and real timings need additional evidence.

items.explanation: Big-O is a mathematical bound under a cost model. State tightness, case and measured behavior separately.
